title: What Did Nvidia’s Board Know, and When?
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

The transcript tells the story of an alleged leadership crisis at Nvidia in November 2026. It says cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged marital infidelity in an email to employees without identifying the other person. Nvidia’s board initially backed him while commissioning an independent investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. According to the transcript, the board said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security had been compromised.

That inquiry centered on Huang’s reported ties to a former executive at Mega Speed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. The transcript describes allegations that a network of companies helped move billions of dollars in Nvidia chips amid U.S. export restrictions. It also says U.S. officials suspected the executive of passing information to Chinese intelligence, an allegation China denied.

The transcript identifies a separate report about Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s longtime healthcare vice president and a direct report to Huang, as the turning point. It says former employees described a hotel recording from Nvidia’s March developer conference and alleged that the person who filmed it was offered a nondisclosure agreement. The transcript says The New York Times had never seen the recording. It also says Powell did not comment and Nvidia declined to confirm the alleged relationship.

According to the account, Huang resigned, CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO, and longtime director Harvey C. Jones became board chair. Powell withdrew from a scheduled healthcare panel in Washington.

The narrative argues that the allegations involving a direct report raised questions about conflicts of interest, the CEO’s authority over an employee’s career, and how Nvidia handled potential misconduct. It leaves open whether directors knew about the reported hotel incident before November. It also highlights how public scrutiny fell on Powell despite Huang’s greater authority and her years building Nvidia’s healthcare business.
